steps.title: The first day
steps.body: A French class in Ottawa. Anna lives in Montréal and Sam lives in Toronto. They meet for the first time.

examples.en: Anna: Hi! My name is Anna.
Sam: Hi! My name is Sam. Nice to meet you.
Anna: Nice to meet you. I live in Montréal.

examples.fr: J'habite à Toronto. Je parle anglais.
examples.en: Sam: I live in Toronto. I speak English.

examples.fr: Oui. Je parle un peu français.
examples.en: Sam: Yes. I speak a little French.
Anna: Me too. Are you Canadian?

examples.fr: Oui, je suis canadien. Et toi ?
examples.en: Sam: Yes, I am Canadian. And you?

examples.fr: Je suis indienne. Je viens de l'Inde.
examples.en: Anna: I am Indian. I come from India.

steps.title: Tip
steps.body: toi is the stressed form of tu: Et toi ? means And you? (informal). The formal form is Et vous ?. The pair moi / toi is used after et and alone: Moi aussi.

steps.title: At the counter
steps.body: A service desk in a government office. The clerk uses vous.

examples.fr: Bonjour, madame. Votre nom, s'il vous plaît ?
examples.en: Agent: Hello, madam. Your name, please?
Agent: Thank you. Are you Canadian?

examples.fr: Non, je suis haïtienne. J'habite à Gatineau.
examples.en: Mme Diallo: No, I am Haitian. I live in Gatineau.
